title: Global sections of CE totals commute with the fixed resolution comparison
statement: For a scheme $X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], a bounded-below complex $K$ of abelian étale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and a termwise hypercohomology presentation $D$ [def-weil-pbc-termwise-hypercohomology-presentation], write $A=\operatorname{Tot}(I)$ and $B=\operatorname{Tot}(\Gamma(X,I))$ after extension and index flip [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation, def-sp-double-complex-total]. The finite-diagonal isomorphism $e_D:B\cong\Gamma(X,A)$, uniquely specified on each diagonal inclusion by the extension comparisons, satisfies $e_D\circ\Gamma(X,D.\mathrm{comparison})=D.w$. For a morphism $f:Y\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and a chain map $g:f^{-1}A\to A\prime$, the degreewise sections unit followed by $\Gamma(Y,g)$ is a chain map, and its postcomposition with $\Gamma(Y,h)$ equals the sections lift of $g\circ h$. These are constructions, not arbitrary existence choices.

proof.text: Obtain the comparison isomorphism and its summand formula from the proved finite-diagonal comparison. The formula uniquely determines its morphism in every degree, so this choice introduces no undetermined data.

On each nonnegative resolution summand, compose the summand equation with global sections of D.comparison, use functoriality, and rewrite using D.w_formula. In negative resolution degree, extension by zero makes the summand zero. Apply total coproduct extensionality in each degree, then chain-map extensionality.

Construct ceSectionsUnit by composing the global-sections/terminal-sections comparison, the inverse-image adjunction unit whiskered by terminal sections, the pushforward/terminal-sections comparison whiskered by upperStar, and the inverse global-sections comparison whiskered by upperStar. Its components are definitionally the prescribed globalSectionsUpperStarMap. Apply its naturality field to each differential and use the chain-map equation of g to construct ceSectionsLift with explicit degree components. Postcomposition follows degreewise from Functor.map_comp and associativity.
